issues.legal_issue: A long-standing High Court interpretation of a local statute should normally be followed by a superior court when disturbing it would unsettle settled law and transactions.
material_facts: Two Full Bench decisions of the High Court had interpreted the relevant provisions of the local tenancy statute and had established the principles governing mortgages of occupancy holdings and recovery of possession.
The parties did not challenge the correctness of those established principles, and transactions might have been entered into in reliance on them.
issues.conclusion: The Court followed the Full Bench decisions, holding that the doctrine of stare decisis should be applied and that the established interpretation should not be disturbed.
issues.legal_principle: In interpreting a local statute, a superior court should normally adhere to a High Court interpretation followed over a number of years where a different view would create uncertainty or unsettle transactions. The Court relied on the Full Bench decisions in Ghassu v. Babu Ram and Mahabal Singh v. Ram Rai, and referred to Brownsea Haven Properties v. Poole Corporation.

rule.if: local_statute_interpretation_case and longstanding_high_court_interpretation and (reliance_transactions_possible or unsettled_law_would_create_uncertainty)

predicates.local_statute_interpretation_case: The case asks a superior court to interpret a local statute on an issue previously addressed by a High Court.
predicates.longstanding_high_court_interpretation: The High Court has followed an interpretation of the statute over a number of years.
predicates.reliance_transactions_possible: People may have arranged transactions in reliance on the established interpretation.
predicates.unsettled_law_would_create_uncertainty: A different interpretation would introduce uncertainty or confusion into the law.

issues.definition: When a case concerns a local statute and the High Court has long applied an interpretation on which transactions may have relied or whose displacement would create uncertainty, the established interpretation should be followed.

issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee's prolonged possession under a void usufructuary mortgage of an occupancy holding does not extinguish the right to recover the holding by paying the mortgage consideration.
material_facts: An occupancy tenant executed a usufructuary mortgage over the holding and put the mortgagee in possession.
The mortgagee and the mortgagee's successors remained in possession for more than twelve years.
The later holders of the occupancy rights sought possession and deposited the mortgage money in court.
issues.conclusion: The mortgagee's status was analogous to that of a mortgagee, and prolonged possession did not extinguish the right to recover possession on payment of the mortgage money; the suit was not barred by time.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principles established in the Full Bench decisions in Ghassu v. Babu Ram and Mahabal Singh v. Ram Rai, a usufructuary mortgage of an occupancy holding is void, but the person in possession is analogous to a mortgagee. Possession for more than twelve years does not extinguish the mortgagor's right to recover the holding on payment of the consideration; it only amounts to prescribing for mortgagee rights. The Court considered sections 33, 44, 45, 82 and 180 of the U.P. Tenancy Act, 1939, and followed the established local interpretation under the doctrine of stare decisis.

rule.if: occupancy_holding_redemption_suit and usufructuary_mortgage_created and mortgagee_possession_over_twelve_years and redemption_money_tendered

predicates.occupancy_holding_redemption_suit: The proceeding seeks recovery of an occupancy holding by redeeming an earlier mortgage.
predicates.usufructuary_mortgage_created: An occupancy tenant gave possession of the holding under a usufructuary mortgage.
predicates.mortgagee_possession_over_twelve_years: The mortgagee or the mortgagee's successors remained in possession for more than twelve years.
predicates.redemption_money_tendered: The person seeking recovery tendered or deposited the money received under the mortgage.

issues.definition: If a recovery proceeding concerns an occupancy holding given into possession under a usufructuary mortgage, the mortgagee remained in possession for more than twelve years, and the redemption money is tendered, the successor may recover possession on repayment.

issues.legal_issue: A person who later acquires occupancy rights in a mortgaged holding and has an interest in that holding may sue to redeem it.
material_facts: The original occupancy tenant's rights ended when later holders were accepted as occupancy tenants of the same holding under a compromise decree.
Those later holders were declared to be bhumidars of the holding.
They brought the suit to recover the holding from the mortgagee's successors after depositing the mortgage money.
issues.conclusion: The later occupancy tenants and bhumidars had sufficient interest in the holding to sue for redemption, and the fact that they were not the original mortgagor did not bar their suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 91(a) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 permits a person other than the mortgagee who has an interest in the mortgaged property, or in the right to redeem it, to sue for redemption. The Court held that the later holders' occupancy and bhumidari interests gave them sufficient interest; the Full Bench principles in Ghassu v. Babu Ram and Mahabal Singh v. Ram Rai supported recovery by a successor to the original mortgagor.

predicates.redemption_suit: The proceeding seeks redemption of a mortgage and recovery of the mortgaged holding.
predicates.claimant_is_not_mortgagee: The person bringing the suit is not the mortgagee of the interest sought to be redeemed.
predicates.claimant_has_interest_in_mortgaged_holdi: The claimant holds an occupancy, ownership, or other legally recognized interest in the mortgaged holding.

issues.definition: In a redemption suit, a claimant who is not the mortgagee may sue for redemption if the claimant has an interest in the mortgaged holding.

issues.legal_issue: A civil court may hear a suit to recover an occupancy holding by redemption where established High Court authority recognizes that forum.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sued in a civil court to recover the holding by paying the mortgage money.
The defendants argued that the suit could be tried only by a revenue court, but that objection had not been raised in the written statement or in the trial court or first appellate court.
A Full Bench decision of the High Court had held that such a suit was maintainable in a civil court.
issues.conclusion: The Court saw no cogent ground to disturb the established High Court view that the suit was maintainable in a civil court.
issues.legal_principle: The Full Bench decision in Mahabal Singh v. Ram Rai held that a suit to recover an occupancy holding by redemption is maintainable in a civil court. The Court applied its principle of adhering to a long-standing High Court interpretation of a local statute and noted that the forum objection had not been raised in the lower courts.

predicates.occupancy_holding_redemption_suit: The proceeding seeks recovery of an occupancy holding by redeeming an earlier mortgage.
predicates.longstanding_high_court_civil_forum_prec: A long-standing High Court decision recognizes that a civil court may hear this kind of suit.

issues.definition: A civil court may hear a suit to recover an occupancy holding by redemption when established High Court authority recognizes that forum.
